newsitem.title: USA: EPA plan focuses on big power plants.
newsitem.headline: EPA plan focuses on big power plants.

text.p: New air quality standards endorsed by President Clinton focus on major power plants to address the long-distance transport of ozone polltion, the White House said.
"This plan focuses on major power plants, which offer the most cost-effective opportunities for reducing pollution to reduce nitrogen oxide, a key ingredient of smog," a White House statement said.
Under the plan, the EPA will let states and counties participating in a regional pollution control strategy have until at least 2004 to meet the new standard, the White House said.

Because the new standard would regulate fine particulates for the first time, EPA will allow five years to build a nationwide monitoring network and to gather and analyze the data needed to designate areas and develop implementation plans, the White House said.
EPA administrator Carol Browner said the new plan amounted to "a major step forward for protecting the public health of the people of this country."
The EPA plan includes a more flexible 24-hour standard of 65 micrograms of particulates per cubic meter, revised from the original EPA proposal of 50 micrograms per cubic meter.
The White House said the new standard will provide new protections to nearly 70 million Americans, and will prevent about 15,000 premature deaths each year.
